description: What a street-level observation says about one building's shape and colour.

visible.instructions: The observation clearly describes a single building's exterior.

criteria.true: One building's walls or roof are described well enough to judge its shape or colour.
criteria.false: No building, several indistinguishable buildings, or only an interior is described.

roof_shape.instructions: Which roof shape does the building have?

criteria.flat: No visible slope; possibly a parapet.
criteria.gable: Two slopes meeting at a ridge, with triangular walls at the two ends.
criteria.hip: Slopes on all four sides, including pyramid and mansard roofs.
criteria.unknown: The roof cannot be seen or judged.

floors.instructions: How many above-ground floors does the building have?

criteria.unknown: The number of floors cannot be judged.

wall_colour.instructions: What is the main colour of the building's walls?

criteria.white: White or near-white render or paint.
criteria.beige: Beige, sand, or light tan stone.
criteria.dark: Black, charcoal, or very dark brown.
criteria.unknown: The wall colour cannot be judged.

criteria.dark: Dark grey or black slate, shingles, or metal.
criteria.green: Green, including copper patina or a planted roof.
criteria.unknown: The roof colour cannot be judged.
